attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet in his signed GPT-5 hot take post.

semantics.note: Faithful. It keeps 'almost 3 years', 'many billions' and 'over a half-trillion fieldwide' and adds no development start date. It is a retrospective factual observation.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. It allows either the ChatGPT or the GPT-4 baseline, sets no strict tolerance and needs US$500B+ of actual fieldwide spending. The result depends on the unstated baseline, the field boundary and the accounting basis.

evidence.note: OpenAI page dated 2022-11-30 confirming ChatGPT's release, one possible baseline. It says nothing about when GPT-5 work began.
OpenAI page dated 2023-03-14 confirming GPT-4's release, an alternative baseline that Marcus did not choose.
OpenAI page confirming the 2025-08-07 endpoint. Elapsed time is 981 days from ChatGPT (about 2 years 8 months) or 877 days from GPT-4. That fits 'almost 3' loosely, but only with a chosen baseline.
Epoch estimates OpenAI spent billions on compute in 2024, roughly $5B of it on R&D. That fits 'many billions' company-wide but allocates nothing to GPT-5 and gives no fieldwide total.

reviews.rationale: The elapsed time (about 2.7 years from ChatGPT) roughly fits 'almost 3 years' on a plausible baseline. OpenAI's multibillion-dollar 2024 compute spending is consistent with 'many billions', but none of it is allocated to GPT-5. Nothing in the packet establishes cumulative fieldwide AI spending above US$500B by launch. The support condition needs every component, so the claim cannot be scored as supported. Nothing contradicts it either.

attribution.note: Marcus's own opening sentence in his signed post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge 'appears' and the reference to his earlier predictions. It is a tentative launch-day impression, not a categorical finding.

contract.note: The contract is right that 'appear' makes this a tentative impression with no objective standard. Scoring it as a categorical claim would make his words stronger than he wrote them.

reviews.rationale: The statement is hedged ('appear to have been solved') and gives no standard for when a problem counts as solved. Under policy, hedged statements like this are not scored, so the outcome is not_adjudicable. The packet contains no evidence items. The case is not broken.
